extracted.intended_audience: writers applying to the Sewanee Writers' Conference (prospective applicants in fiction, poetry, nonfiction, playwriting)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and requirements for applying to the Sewanee Writers' Conference (July 14–26, 2026), including eligibility, deadlines, submission categories, attendance expectations, tuition/aid policy, and post-acceptance manuscript/workshop procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference dates
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dates indicate the period applicants should plan to attend if accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — age requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be 21 years of age by the time of the Conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond this criterion, age is not a factor in admissions; the conference welcomes a wide range of ages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission categories / multiple-category applications allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers may apply to the Sewanee Writers' Conference by submitting applications in one or more of the categories listed below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categories listed on the page: FICTION, POETRY, NONFICTION, PLAYWRITING. Applicants may submit to multiple categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All participants are expected to attend the Conference for its entire 12-day duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full participation for the entire conference is an expectation of acceptances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification date
rubrics_metrics.description: All applicants will be notified of decisions via email April 15.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-acceptance manuscript/workshop submission and faculty choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants accepted to the Conference will have the opportunity to submit a separate manuscript for workshop as well as their top choices for a faculty reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted applicants can provide a separate workshop manuscript and indicate preferred faculty readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tuition, room, board, and financial-aid policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Tuition, room, and board will now be $3,000 for all participants; $3,000 is 40% of the actual cost to attend, so every writer will receive 60% support to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The conference has shifted away from publication/production-based fellowships and scholarships toward need-based aid; all participants will have the same reading time, status, and opportunities as part of an egalitarian approach driven by budgetary considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty roster (who will be teaching/reading)
rubrics_metrics.description: 2026 Faculty listed by genre (e.g., FICTION: Chris Bachelder, Sarah Shun-lien Bynum, Lydi Conklin, Amitava Kumar, Margot Livesey, Jill McCorkle, Claire Messud, Chinelo Okparanta, Maurice Carlos Ruffin, Stephanie Powell Watts; POETRY: Marianne Chan, Eduardo C. Corral, Danielle Cadena Deulen, Ananda Lima, Carl Phillips, Caki Wilkinson; NONFICTION: Jaquira Díaz, Amy Leach, Alex Marzano-Lesnevich, Elena Passarello; PLAYWRITING: Nathan Alan Davis, Dan O'Brien, Anne Washburn, Lauren Yee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides applicants information about faculty who will be present and from whom they may request readers or workshops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current submission status
rubrics_metrics.description: There are presently no open calls for submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that at the time of viewing, applicants cannot submit because no open calls are posted.
